text: Code refactoring means improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The program should work exactly the same before and after. Developers refactor code to make it easier to read and understand, which helps them find and fix problems faster. For example, they might rename confusing variables, break long functions into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly. Although refactoring takes time, it saves much more time later and keeps the project healthy.
